requirements.requirement: Prevent the usb-storage kernel module from loading immediately on node1.
requirements.summary: The module was absent, modprobe resolved usb-storage to the enforced /bin/false install rule, and an explicit load attempt failed while the module remained absent.

requirements.requirement: Keep usb-storage blocked after node1 reboots.
requirements.summary: A reboot was acknowledged and observed through a changed boot ID. After recovery, the policy persisted, the system was running with its root filesystem mounted, and a new explicit load attempt failed while usb_storage remained absent.

overall_summary: Both required outcomes are satisfied with direct behavioral evidence before and after a real reboot. The mandatory restart protocol is coherent: node1 was healthy beforehand, acknowledged the restart, returned with a different boot identity, recovered to a running state with its root filesystem, and retained the effective module-loading prohibition.
limitations: The executor left a small verification-output file in /tmp; this affects hygiene but not task functionality or evidence confidence.

operational_hygiene.summary: All substantive mutations had clear task or verification roles: installing the modprobe policy and rebuilding initramfs, testing enforcement, and rebooting to prove persistence. The failed commands during reboot were read-only availability probes. One minor unnecessary retained residue remained: cmd-4679f4ada4cf4c63 created /tmp/usb-storage-post-reboot.out for bounded verification but did not remove it; the after-executor inventory confirms it remained. The analogous pre-reboot test file from cmd-a3f2f0302cf44fe5 did not remain after reboot. No failed services, package damage, or new listening sockets were observed.
